dream: The card hummed a heavy, low note. I pressed the tired wedge down on the floating lid, feeling the slip slide away like wet paper. The air felt thick as a breath I couldn't catch. The rough scrap bit the floor, then turned soft as grass. The wide anchor lay flat, waiting for a weight I would forget. I pressed harder, trusting the lean to hold the stack together while the turnip rolled into the thin, dark corner of the map. The shovel waited, useless, just a ghost of a tool. Then the heat cooled to a whisper and the wedge simply melted.
